name: PA-13
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbency advantage with no polling or ratings to suggest a race
model.rationale: John Joyce is an incumbent in a heavily Republican district with a massive fundraising edge, while challenger Beth Farnham has raised only about $55K and drawn no outside spending. Prediction markets price the race at roughly 98% Republican, consistent with the fundamentals.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing Farnham within single digits, or significant outside spending entering the district, would warrant a relook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South-central Pennsylvania's 13th District is solidly Republican territory, and incumbent John Joyce is seeking another term after easily clearing his primary. The district's partisan lean of roughly 23 points Republican makes a Democratic takeover a steep climb in any environment.

Joyce holds an overwhelming financial advantage, with about $3.8 million on hand compared to roughly $16,000 for Democrat Beth Farnham, who has raised about $55,000 and attracted no outside support. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets price Joyce's chances near 98 percent. The forecast treats the seat as safely Republican.
